title: PGE, British Columbia Railway and BC Rail — verified history research

sources.title: An Act to incorporate the Pacific Great Eastern Railway Company (1912, c.36)
claims: PGE incorporated 27 February 1912.
Intended railway ran to a junction with Grand Trunk Pacific at or near Fort George.

sources.title: 1912 agreement-ratification Act, chapter 34
claims: GTP and PGE promoters agreed on construction and reciprocal traffic routing.
GTP had a conditional first right to acquire control; this is not evidence PGE was a GTP subsidiary.

sources.title: Howe Sound, Pemberton Valley and Northern Railway Company incorporation Act (1907, c.53)
claims: Original legal name was The Howe Sound, Pemberton Valley & Northern Railway Company.

sources.title: The Beginnings of the Pacific Great Eastern Railway — Whistler Museum
sources.locator: Body text, predecessor and 1912 takeover paragraphs
claims: Existing Howe Sound railway was taken over by Foley, Welch & Stewart in 1912.
Treat this as predecessor undertaking/acquisition, not necessarily continuation of its legal corporation.

sources.title: British Columbia Railway Act (1972, c.8)
claims: PGE's legal name changed to British Columbia Railway Company.
The statute preserved rights, liabilities and property: corporate continuity.

sources.title: Canadian Rail 248, September 1972
sources.locator: Printed p.265 / PDF p.5: April 1 change; printed p.278 / PDF p.18: new dogwood caption; PDF p.19: car photograph
claims: Contemporary report dates public British Columbia Railway name to 1 April 1972.
Dogwood described as the new corporate symbol; photograph credited to BCR.

sources.title: Environmental Appeal Board decision 2000-WAS-018(b)
sources.locator: PDF pp.3–4, Corporate History of the BCR Group
claims: Province became PGE's sole shareholder in 1918.
BCR Properties incorporated 18 May 1984; S.C. Holdings renamed BC Rail 28 May; assets transferred 12 June.
BCR Partnership created 5 December 1997.
sources.caution: Narrative incorrectly calls the 1972 legal name 'Corporation'; use the statute's 'Company'.

sources.title: 1985 Report of the Auditor General of British Columbia
sources.locator: PDF pp.110–111, note 8(c), and PDF p.166, note 8(b)
claims: BC Harbours Board assets transferred to BC Development Corporation and BCR effective 31 October 1983.
The railway assets went to BCR.
sources.caution: Filename misleadingly says 1984; actual report title is 1985, reviewing fiscal year ended 31 March 1984.

sources.title: CIPO trademark application 0770811: BC RAIL
claims: Applicant claimed BC RAIL word use for services since 18 May 1984.
Filed 1994; application later abandoned.
sources.caution: Supports wording only, not the precise graphic logo, colours or date of a particular graphic design.

sources.title: BC government: $1-billion investment partnership agreement released
sources.locator: 12 August 2004; agreement descriptions and closing paragraph
claims: Formal closing with CN occurred 14 July 2004.
BC Rail Ltd shares and BCR Partnership units transferred to CN; publicly owned track/right-of-way made available for freight operations.

sources.title: Transportation Safety Board railway investigation R05V0141
claims: TSB dates CN acquisition of the BCR system to 15 July 2004.
sources.caution: Use July 14 for legal closing and July 15 for operational transition, explaining the distinction.

sources.title: BCTFA consolidated financial statements, year ended 31 March 2021
claims: BCRC became a wholly owned BCTFA subsidiary on 1 April 2010.

sources.title: BCRC consolidated financial statements, year ended 31 March 2025
claims: BCRC remains owned by BCTFA.
Retains former BC Rail right-of-way and track infrastructure leased to CN.
Retains Port Subdivision operation serving Roberts Bank and BCR Properties subsidiary activities.

sources.title: The Cariboo, Issue Three, January 1991; Greg M. Kennelly, Logos of the Pacific Great Eastern Railway
sources.locator: PDF pp. 5–8: Greg M. Kennelly’s logo history; p. 1: newsletter masthead; p. 14: PGE colour and livery diagrams
claims: Logo article expands the author's September–October and November–December 1986 Coupler articles with information supplied by former railway employees.
sources.caution: Use local uploaded source for detailed logo chronology. Do not treat observed photograph dates as introduction dates or stated rumours as events.

sources.title: Central BC Railway and Forestry Museum — History
claims: PGE reached Prince George in 1952.
GTP reached Prince George in 1914 and became part of CN, a distinct line from PGE.

sources.title: Canadian Rail 547, March–April 2012
sources.locator: Printed p.49 / PDF p.5: BC Rail name date; p.70 / PDF p.26: BCR dogwood; p.72 / PDF p.28: red-blue BC Rail graphic
claims: Brief overview dates BC Rail public name to 19 June 1984.
sources.caution: Article oversimplifies retained railway ownership after 2004; use provincial audited financial statements for legal ownership.

sources.title: The Cariboo 23, January 1996; Ron Tuff, B.C.R.'s Wide Vision Cabooses, diagrams Greg M. Kennelly
claims: A white BC RAIL herald was specified on caboose diagrams dated 19 February 1985.
A proposed July 1986 caboose scheme used a new red-blue BC RAIL herald; the implemented final caboose scheme was documented 11 March 1987.
sources.caution: Equipment-specific scheme dates do not establish first company-wide graphic use. Diagrams are Kennelly reconstructions, not original company artwork; do not represent them as masters.

sources.title: PGE RCC2 logo detail, North Vancouver, circa 1970 — Chuck Strawn Collection
claims: Archival original photograph of PGE equipment logo, dated circa 1970.

sources.title: British Columbia Railway Company official website
sources.locator: Corporate wordmark; existing gallery specimen collected 22 October 2026
claims: The continuing provincial company uses its own BC Railway Company wordmark. The website asset does not establish a design introduction date.

exclusions: Do not equate BCRC's legal history with BC Rail Ltd's operating history.
Do not treat CIPO word-mark application 0770811 as graphic-design evidence.
CW Railway general history incorrectly says sold in 2002; use primary 2004 records.
Old BC Archives Time Machine account confuses provincial acquisition and Prince George arrival dates.
A first known dated photograph proves use by that date, not the design's launch date.
Reporting marks BCOL/BCIT are not separate corporate entities or proof of logo rollout.
Do not date familiar red-blue BC Rail graphic to 1984 merely from name change. Cariboo 23 distinguishes the white 1985 herald and a newer red-blue herald in 1986/87 caboose diagrams.
